skill.name: axiom-audit
skill.description: Audit Axiom logs, prioritize errors and warnings, research probable causes, and flag log quality issues.
skill.summary: Audit Axiom logs and produce prioritized, evidence-based incident reports.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby or shell backtick alerts are Markdown fences or inline examples, but several bash blocks do require external CLI installation and Axiom MCP execution. The sensitive finding is confirmed because the skill instructs searching .env and config files for Axiom credentials. Additional concerns include unpinned tool installation and credential discovery guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the grep command for .env and config files. Ask users to provide AXIOM_TOKEN through approved secret management instead.
Pin known-good versions or direct users to official installation documentation before enabling the skill.

remediation.issue: External command execution with Axiom access
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running mcp, go, brew, or grep commands. Show the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: Sensitive log data in generated reports
remediation.suggestion: Redact tokens, PII, and complete raw log payloads before writing or sharing audit reports.

content.value_statement: Production logs can hide urgent errors, noisy warnings, and weak logging practices. This skill queries Axiom, prioritizes issues, and creates an evidence-based audit report.
actual_capabilities: Lists Axiom datasets through the configured axiom-mcp server.
Queries recent errors, warnings, and trends with APL examples.
Ranks issues by severity and frequency using P0 to P4 scoring.
Researches probable causes by reading related project code.
Creates a Markdown audit report under .audits.
Flags log smells such as sensitive data exposure and missing context.
limitations: Requires Axiom credentials and local MCP tooling before use.
Can read project files while researching errors.
May surface sensitive log data if logs contain secrets or PII.
Does not fix code defects; it only reports findings.

use_cases.title: Production Incident Triage
use_cases.description: Identify the highest-priority errors and warnings from recent Axiom logs during an incident.

use_cases.title: Observability Quality Review
use_cases.description: Find noisy logs, missing context, vague messages, and sensitive data exposure risks.

use_cases.title: Release Health Audit
use_cases.description: Review new or increasing errors after a release and summarize probable causes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Error Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit for recent production errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use axiom-audit to review the last 24 hours of Axiom logs. Prioritize errors and warnings, then summarize P0 and P1 issues.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Dataset
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the right dataset before querying.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use axiom-audit to list available Axiom datasets. Choose the likely production log dataset and explain your choice before querying.

prompt_templates.title: Research Root Causes
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect recurring log patterns to code evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use axiom-audit to group recurring errors from the last 7 days. Research related code and identify probable causes with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Executive Audit Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report with trends and log quality findings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use axiom-audit to create a full audit report for the last 7 days. Include trends, log smells, source evidence, and remediation priorities.

output_examples.output: Returns a ranked summary of top errors, affected areas, likely causes, and a link to the generated audit report.

output_examples.input: Find noisy warnings in Axiom logs.
output_examples.output: Highlights repeated warning messages, estimated volume, missing context, and recommended owner for follow-up.

output_examples.input: Review log quality before a release.
output_examples.output: Lists sensitive data exposures, generic messages, missing stack traces, and other log smells with priority labels.

best_practices: Confirm the target dataset and time range before running broad queries.
Use read-only credentials with the narrowest Axiom scope available.
Review generated reports before sharing them outside the incident team.
anti_patterns: Do not search repository secret files unless the user explicitly asks.
Do not paste raw tokens, PII, or complete log dumps into reports.
Do not treat frequency alone as severity without code or business context.

faq.question: Does this skill modify application code?
faq.answer: No. It only audits logs and can write a Markdown report.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It expects axiom-mcp, mcptools, Axiom credentials, and shell access.

faq.question: Can it work without Axiom credentials?
faq.answer: No. It needs a valid token to query Axiom datasets.

faq.question: Does it detect sensitive data in logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explicitly checks for log smells such as PII, secrets, and tokens.

faq.question: Is it safe for production logs?
faq.answer: Use read-only credentials and limit time ranges. Review outputs for sensitive data before sharing.

faq.question: Can it fix the errors it finds?
faq.answer: No. It identifies probable causes and priorities, but it does not change code.
